title: Developer Experimentation Harness PRD — scenario-driven cost & fidelity sandbox
author: Sofia Kim
summary:
Short intro:
The Developer Experimentation Harness (DEH) is a self-serve sandbox and simulation layer that lets engineers and product teams run reproducible consumption scenarios against Redwood inference surfaces. DEH enables cost/latency/fidelity trade-off experiments, tenant-flavored presets, and deterministic regressions for rollout safety before customers change production routing or pricing. This PRD defines scope, success metrics, API/UI surface, telemetry needs, and a staged rollout plan.
background_and_problem_statement:
Background:
Teams building inference features need a low-friction way to quantify the end-to-end economics of configuration changes (batching, quantization, KV cache policies, model fallbacks) without provisioning dedicated capacity or risking customer SLAs. Existing tools are siloed: offline simulators lack realistic KV/cache dynamics; production canaries are expensive and slow to analyze. Problem statement:
- Engineers need reproducible scenarios that reflect realistic token distributions and session patterns.
- Product owners need cost and fidelity deltas tied to variant metadata for commercial decisions.
- Platform teams need telemetry contracts so simulation outputs map to runtime metrics and billing attribution.
goals:
Primary goals:
1) Provide a self-serve UI + CLI to create, run, and share scenario runs that model throughput, latency, and cost across hosted/dedicated/private variants.
2) Offer preset scenario templates (chat-heavy, transactional, long-context, embeddings-batch) with tenant-aware seeds.
3) Surface a standardized report that shows per-route expected tokens, median/99th latency, KV hit/miss ratios, estimated per-1M-token cost, and fidelity delta (from eval prompt-sets).
4) Integrate with Optimize suggestions to propose config changes and estimate projected savings.
Success metrics (90 days after GA):
- 25 internal teams have run >= 5 scenario experiments each.
- Median scenario runtime < 10 minutes for a representative 1M-token sim.
- Fidelity regression detection rate >= 95% on seeded prompt-sets.
non_goals:
Out of scope for initial launch:
- Full chargeable billing for simulated runs (simulations are metered for internal usage only).
- Automated production rollout of recommended config changes (we will only produce recommendations and an operator checklist).
- Support for every third-party model adapter — initial adapters limited to Redwood-verified variants.
user_personas:
Primary personas:
- ML Engineer (internal): runs experiments to validate quantization and KV-cache changes.
- Backend Engineer / Platform Owner: compares latency profiles across deployment types to decide regional routing.
- Product Manager: evaluates trade-offs between cost and quality for pricing tiers.
- Solutions Engineer / Customer Success: prepares customer-facing economic impact reports for Dedicated migration.
requirements_matrix:
Requirements (ID | Description | Priority | Acceptance Criteria | Owner):
REQ-001 | Scenario definition language (YAML/JSON) and presets for session patterns | P0 | Create scenario file, run locally and see matching runtime summary | Eng-Developer-Experience
REQ-002 | Kernel of the simulator must model KV cache hit/miss with configurable warmup and TTL | P0 | Simulated KV hit/miss within 5% of small production sample | Eng-Serving-Runtime
REQ-003 | Cost model exporter that converts simulator tokens/compute to per-variant cost estimates using current price signals | P0 | Exported cost delta matches historical invoice-derived estimates within 10% | Finance-Led; Eng-Data
REQ-004 | Fidelity delta measurement: run prompt-sets and compute BLEU/ROUGE/Answer-accuracy deltas vs baseline | P1 | Regression flagging and sample counterexample output | Applied-ML-and-Evals
REQ-005 | UI run history, shareable link, and JSON export for reports | P1 | Save/Share/Download works and persists for 90 days | Eng-Developer-Experience
REQ-006 | Integrate with Optimize to surface config suggestions and projected savings | P1 | Optimize suggestions appear in report with confidence band | Product/Optimize
REQ-007 | Telemetry contract: align simulator metrics to runtime telemetry names and tag keys | P0 | Mapping doc and a validation run that asserts metric parity | Eng-Platform
REQ-008 | RBAC: only whitelisted internal teams may run high-fidelity tenant-anchored scenarios | P1 | Enforcement via Console ACLs and CLI auth | Security-and-Compliance
REQ-009 | CI gate: harness must be runnable in CI with stable seed for regression detection | P1 | PRs can include scenario runs and fail on regressions | Eng-DevEx
REQ-010 | Runtime fast-mode: approximate sim with sampling for quicker iteration | P2 | Fast-mode completes within 2 minutes for 100k-token profile | Eng-Serving-Runtime
high_level_design_and_architecture:
Overview:
DEH has three logical components: Scenario Composer (UI/CLI), Simulation Engine, and Result Analyzer + Reporter.
Scenario Composer:
- Web-based builder with preset templates and an advanced YAML editor.
- CLI: 'rdeh run --scenario my-chat.yaml --variant hosted-1'
Simulation Engine:
- Pluggable runtime adapters (hosted, dedicated emulator, private-local proxy).
- Event-driven session player that replays token streams, models KV requests, batching, and quantization routing.
- Two execution modes: fidelity-mode (deterministic, full KV) and fast-mode (sampled, probabilistic).
Result Analyzer + Reporter:
- Normalizes outputs to standard metric names (rdeh.metrics.*) and runs fidelity evals.
- Produces PDF/JSON summary and creates a Console report accessible via shareable link.
Data flow:
1) User uploads scenario -> 2) Composer sends to Engine -> 3) Engine emits runtime metrics to analysis service -> 4) Analyzer computes cost/fidelity deltas and stores run snapshot.
api_and_cli_examples:
Example: scenario YAML snippet:
---
scenario_name: tenant-chat-transactional
sessions:
  - count: 1000
    pattern: conversational
    avg_turns: 6
    token_distribution: "short-tail"
model_variants:
  - hosted-v2
  - dedicated-quantized-v1
kv_cache:
  warmup_percent: 10
  ttl_seconds: 3600
---
CLI run example:
$ rdeh run --scenario tenant-chat-transactional.yaml --target hosted-v2 --mode fidelity --output report.json
API:
POST /api/v1/simulations  
Headers: Authorization: Bearer <token>
Body: { "scenario_yaml": "<encoded>", "target_variant": "hosted-v2", "mode": "fidelity" }
Response: { "run_id": "sim-20261130-01", "status": "pending" }
telemetry_and_metrics_contract:
Core metrics emitted by Simulation Engine (naming conventions):
- rdeh.sim.tokens.generated (count)
- rdeh.sim.latency.p50/p95/p99 (ms)
- rdeh.sim.kv.hit_rate (ratio)
- rdeh.sim.batch.size.mean (tokens)
- rdeh.sim.cpu.gpu.ms (ms)
- rdeh.sim.estimated_cost_usd (USD)
- rdeh.sim.fidelity.delta_accuracy (percentage)
Mapping requirements:
- Each simulator metric must include the 'variant' and 'scenario_id' tags.
- Analyzer must produce a 'report.summary' JSON blob that Console can ingest.
- Telemetry retention: internal simulation metrics stored for 180 days; anonymized aggregates for 540 days.
KPIs to track:
- Time-to-first-report, simulated_cost_accuracy_vs_billing, number_of_unique_scenarios_run
acceptance_criteria:
GA acceptance checklist:
- All P0 requirements green.
- 10 representative internal scenarios run and validated vs production traces.
- Console reports render and share links are stable under 100 concurrent viewers.
- Security review complete and RBAC enforced for high-fidelity tenant scenarios.
- User documentation and five how-to templates published.
- Post-launch telemetry shows no more than 2% error rate in metric ingestion over 24h sampling.
rollout_plan_and_milestones:

- Beta (wider internal + selected SE customers) — 2027-02-01 to 2027-03-15: add SRE and Solutions Engineering; collect UX feedback.
- GA (internal + open customers) — 2027-04-01: public docs, training playbook, and Optimize integration.
Milestones:

M2: Analyzer + eval integration — 2027-01-10

M4: Optimize integration and cost-export — 2027-03-01
M5: Security sign-off and GA readiness — 2027-03-20
dependencies_and_risks:
Dependencies:
- Runtime telemetry naming standard (eng-platform): mapping must be finalized by 2026-11-20.
- Optimize API for suggestion handoff (product/optimize).
- Finance pricing signals and cost model (finance).
Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Simulator diverges from production cost because of kernel-level differences. Mitigation: calibrate with weekly production trace samples and maintain a 90-day rolling calibration window.
- Risk: High-fidelity tenant scenarios leak PII. Mitigation: enforce tenant anonymization in the composer and require legal sign-off for tenant-anchored runs.
- Risk: Overlap with existing consumption-sandbox work. Mitigation: alignment syncs and a single ownership charter documented with roadmap owners.
open_questions:
1) What SLA should be guaranteed for analysis report generation in Beta? (Ops input required)
2) Does Finance want simulated runs to appear on billing dashboards as a separate internal ledger?
3) Which Optimize heuristics are safe to expose as automated recommendations vs advisory?
